sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from the selected law \(p=P(E,W,Z\mid S=1)\), with an independent margin multinomial sample in design A when margins are estimated and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one draw of \((E,W,Z)\) conditional on \(S=1\); the finite SCM is a superpopulation model.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is binary and may be confounded with the response type; in design B its assignment probability may depend on \((U,Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All population selected cells are positive. A nonempty supplied-margin fiber forces every population cell margin to be positive. Wald inference additionally requires separated incident charts, common first derivatives, smooth local continuations, and target covariance bounded away from singularity; Hausdorff equivalence of profile and Wald regions also requires a locally saturated compatible observable neighborhood.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced selected-table and independent margin coordinates use empirical multinomial frequencies and the block-diagonal plug-in covariance. The deterministic chart selector uses the stated tolerance and full-square fallback. Transition inference profiles the exact multinomial discrepancy over the complete compatible target fiber and applies Berger--Boos calibration; this gives finite-sample coverage even when chart selection or point identification fails.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 identify PN and PS under positive observed tables, invertible proxy matrices, and unequal determinant-ratio conditions.
Formula (5) identifies a causal effect under a proxy rank condition without identifying the measurement mechanism.
Proposition 3.3 characterizes infinitesimal rigidity of an exact nonnegative factorization by its admissible-motion cone.
Theorems 5--9 give necessary support conditions and sufficient sequential recovery conditions for selected NMF factors.
Theorem 1 gives sufficient positive-scattering thresholds for minimality and uniqueness of nonnegative tensor decompositions.
Theorem 3.4 gives a regular root-n estimator for a linear proximal target without uniqueness of the bridge solution.

Theorem 1 identifies all four response-type probabilities in a randomized experiment under positive conditional tables, \(W\perp Z\mid U\), \(X\perp(U,Z,W)\), invertible cell matrices, and unequal determinant ratios; equations (8)--(11) give plug-in estimators.

Theorem 1 identifies all four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types under Figure 2(b)'s IV-plus-proxy recursive factorization, the five invertibility requirements in condition (i), the cross-treatment second-column separation in condition (ii), and the two exclusion restrictions in condition (iii).

Theorems 2--5 give sound closed-form bounds for a representative family of discrete probabilities of causation from standard experimental and observational distributions, while general-dimensional tightness remains open in the current version.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without strong identification.
E-variable inversion yields exact anytime-valid confidence sets for contingency-table parameters.
Theorem 4 identifies PN and PS under exogeneity and monotonicity, and equations (15)--(18) give sharp bounds otherwise.

body.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, a boundary-complete structural atlas decides PN/PS target rigidity. It exhausts rank-two orientations and the four disjoint rank-one modes, retains equal-endpoint split vectors and inactive rows, and adds response-level residual forests for the unknown-margin relevant-IV design. After chartwise compatibility tests, one feasible cycle point is sampled and each chart is tested for a different target by one-copy existential realizability. The output is an exact common target, two legal same-observable SCMs, or model incompatibility; connected-component enumeration and target projection are optional diagnostics. The selected-law model is the finite four-response-type specialization of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki Condition 1: design A is its fixed-margin subfiber and design B is its equation-(13) IV subclass plus relevance. Theorem 1 transfers by restriction in design A and Corollary 1 transfers directly in design B. The contribution is the strict compatible singular/boundary classification extension, not an extension of those regular formulas. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains universal, while Wald and Hausdorff equivalence remain confined to separated, locally saturated rigid profiles.

project_justification.gap: Published regular proxy formulas identify PN and PS under their rank and separation conditions but do not classify compatible fibers when ranks fall, coefficients reach support faces, endpoints coincide, rows become inactive, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown margins. Generic real-algebraic decidability also hides the response-cycle obstruction and can impose unnecessary decomposition stages.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled cycle whose causal target may be rigid even while nuisance factorizations vary. Exhaustive local edge modes, shared endpoints, and residual forests reduce each legal fiber to a finite union of one-copy semialgebraic charts. One feasible target value then turns global rigidity into one existential disagreement test per chart.
project_justification.fill: The compiler gives necessary and sufficient compatibility and target-agreement tests for supplied-margin and relevant-IV designs. It samples one feasible chart point, tests every chart for a different target, and returns an exact algebraic value or legal full-SCM twins. Its fixed-alphabet termination theorem multiplies the causal chart count by sequential singly-exponential sampling, existential, and encoding bounds, with coefficient-extension degree and rational height propagated in execution order. The statistical layer remains separated-chart Wald inference together with universal finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage.

body.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026) provide the selected response-type model and regular PN/PS formulas. At selected-law factorization level, the present finite model is their Condition-1 four-response-type specialization. The supplied-margin design is a fixed-margin subfiber, so their Theorem 1 transfers by restriction; the unknown-margin IV design is their equation-(13) subclass plus relevance, so their Corollary 1 transfers directly. The atlas agrees on those exact regular overlaps and extends only the compatible classification domain to singular and boundary fibers; it neither extends the regular formulas beyond their hypotheses nor claims blanket subsumption. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) and Kawakami (2021) supply separate regular overlap checks, including a one-law boundary scope separation from Kawakami's invertibility domain. Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work informs the geometry but does not state causal target constancy on this labeled cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the classical singly-exponential critical-point sampling, one-block existential-realizability, primitive-element, Thom-sign, and isolation algorithms used after structural exhaustiveness is proved.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact compiler is a theorem-level symbolic procedure, not a completed production implementation or a favorable growing-alphabet complexity claim. The displayed fixed-alphabet envelope uses published singly-exponential bounds for the executed sampling and existential stages, composed with algebraic coefficient-extension and height bounds; optional connected-component or target-projection diagnostics are excluded. Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. A rational field expression is returned only when constructed; otherwise the exact output remains a real-univariate and Thom encoding. Strictly positive twins are guaranteed only when both sampled cycle witnesses occupy interior support charts. Universal confidence coverage does not imply shrinking at a nonidentified transition, and first-order Hausdorff agreement still requires a locally saturated separated rigid profile. The frozen materials lack the released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds, so no empirical compatibility or rigidity verdict is claimed.
body.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is the exhaustive fixed-alphabet response-cycle classifier and its one-sample, all-chart existential agreement test. Empty fibers are incompatibility and are non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition. The selected model matches the published Condition-1 factorization only at the stated finite four-response-type specialization; design A restricts it by fixed margins, and design B restricts equation (13) by relevance. Published regular values transfer on those precise subfibers, while the new result strictly extends compatible classification to singular and boundary strata without extending the published formula or claiming blanket subsumption. The termination result gives an explicit chart count and sequential sampling, existential, encoding, degree, and rational-height bounds, not favorable growing-alphabet complexity. Wald inference still requires chart separation, common first derivatives, smooth continuations, proportional margin sampling when applicable, and nonsingular target covariance. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains unchanged and universal; its optional Wald-equivalence clause still additionally requires a locally saturated compatible neighborhood. The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and recovery of the released table, not a numerical reanalysis.
